For a general discussion of the management of wounds and ulcers, see p.1585. In a randomised double-blind study in 61 patients with diabetic foot ulcers, adding human epidermal growth factor 0.04% to an ulcer cream containing protein-free bovine blood extract was shown to significantly enhance wound healing and reduce heal- ing time compared with either the cream alone or the cream plus human epidermal growth factor 0.02%.1 Topical application of recombinant human epidermal growth factor 0.02% has also been reported to reduce pain and promote healing of exfoliated skin lesions in a patient with drug-induced Stevens-Johnson syn- drome.2 The effect on the rate of wound healing of a cream containing sulfadiazine silver plus recombinant human epidermal growth factor (10 micrograms/mL) was compared with sulfadiazine sil- ver alone in 12 patients each requiring skin grafts at 2 donor sites.3 The cream containing epidermal growth factor accelerated the rate of epidermal regeneration in all patients and reduced the average time to 100% healing by about 1.5 days. Patients were followed up for a maximum of 1 year after cessation of therapy and no complications or clinical evidence of neoplasia at the healed donor sites occurred.
